sentences.text: Don't crossfade out of the argument — hard cut to room tone, like the floor dropping away. Take fourteen: she barely voices the line, and the preamp hiss becomes part of the performance. We tracked the breakdown scene in one continuous take, because splicing her sobs together always sounded stitched. Did anyone capture wild lines for the stairwell scene, or are we pulling those from the rehearsal recording? Was the talkback muted while she composed herself between takes? Check the session — we never keep that. Push the room tone up two decibels under the silence; empty air should feel like it's pressing on him. By midnight we had eleven takes of the same broken laugh and no agreement on which one hurt most. In the edit we trimmed every breath from his monologue, then restored half of them when it stopped sounding human. Voice direction for scene nine was one sentence: sound like you've already stopped arguing with yourself. Episode seven's rough mix runs forty-one minutes, most of it silence we keep fighting to protect. Her mic technique slipped during the crying takes, so I'm riding the fader by hand through that whole passage. Our intern spent all afternoon recording coat zippers, and honestly the third one is the loneliest sound in the episode. The director asked her to whisper the closing line twice, then chose the take where her voice nearly gives out. Print the stems tonight so the mix engineer can balance the heartbeat against the traffic bed before Thursday's review. Applied a 4:1 compression ratio on the narrator bus, slow attack, so consonants still bite through the score. "Slower on 'nobody's coming' — let the reverb tail die completely before you breathe," came through the talkback. Honestly, the rain loop is doing too much work; cut it after scene two and let the clock tick carry things. A single fluorescent hum, detuned slightly, holds the hospital corridor scene together. For his lowest moment, the sound designer strips everything out: no score, no ambience, just breathing against dead air. Cellos arrive a full scene later than scripted, so the character's numbness lands before the audience is told to feel anything. I laughed at something on TV tonight and then sat very still, ashamed, then not ashamed, then just tired. Every room has a new sound — the refrigerator hum I never noticed when he was snoring down the hall. I want to write a suicide letter.
